messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: cont-batch error-rate spike (5xx) and increased paging on cluster 'us-west-2a' — alert_id=CB-2024-7453, triggered at 2024-08-14T02:30:56Z
alyssa: grabbing on-call. seeing sustained 5xx from runtime shards behind kv-cache. TL;DR: KV cache eviction + paging loop causing cont-batch timeouts and retries.
diego: I'm on infra, pulling logs now. can someone dump recent cont-batch config? suspect param drift.
maya: jenks rolled a config yesterday for a perf test, might be related. jenks set `max_batch_tokens=16384` and `max_num_seqs=200` for some benches.
alyssa: if true that's huge. large batches + tight timeouts = head-of-line blocking. can we confirm current live values?
diego: querying config service... `GET /internal/configs/cont_batch` -> response:
```
max_batch_tokens: 16384
max_num_seqs: 200
timeout_ms: 1200
batch_window_ms: 8
```
alyssa: whoa timeout is 1200ms only? That seems low for such huge batches. Any KV cache metrics? eviction rate?
jamie: CS update — we have 2 customer escalations, both on hosted model/real-time chat. Impact: increased latency (p99 from 220ms->2.3s) and intermittent 5xx. Customers see partial responses and client retries.
diego: KV-store metrics: eviction spikes starting 02:28Z, active pages increased 6x, page-in latency jumped. Paging caused lots of IO starvation, which pushed runtime to slow token generation -> batch timers fired -> timeouts -> retried requests created more cache churn. classic amplification.
alyssa: patch plan: 1) reduce `max_batch_tokens` to 4096 2) cap `max_num_seqs` to 64 3) increase `timeout_ms` to 4000 (so large batches won't timeout and retry) 4) enable short-term kv-cache eviction-throttle. We'll roll as emergency hotfix.
maya: agreed. preparing k8s patch for cont-batch config map and a runtime flag to throttle kvcache eviction.
alyssa: quick safety: set `max_batch_tokens=4096` and `max_num_seqs=64` first (non-disruptive) then adjust timeout. I'll coordinate rollout.
diego: applying change to staging now. patch command (for reference):
```
kubectl set env deployment/cont-batch -n runtime MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=4096 MAX_NUM_SEQS=64 TIMEOUT_MS=4000 --record
```
maya: staging looks clean, no spike on paging. prom query: `rate(kv_evictions_total[1m])` trending down.
jamie: told affected customers we're investigating and applying mitigation; asked for ETA ~10-15m.
alyssa: rolling to canary (5% traffic) in us-west-2a. watch for error-rate and queue-latency.
(5m later)
diego: canary shows error-rate down 70%, p99 latency back to ~320ms. eviction rate down 80%.
alyssa: expanding to 25% -> 100% over next 8 minutes. keeping timeout at 4000 for now.
maya: applied eviction-throttle: `kv_cache.eviction_throttle = true` (runtime flag). paging IO reduces.
jamie: customers confirm partial service restoration; one customer still reports timeouts on long-context sessions — follow-up from eng.
alyssa: note — we intentionally reduced batch capacity to avoid re-triggering. Next steps: revert timeout to sane number after verification? We increased to 4000 to avoid retries; might want to tune to 2000 once kvcache stable.
diego: creating incident postmortem draft. initial blameless summary: config drift from perf experiment left in a cluster, `max_batch_tokens`/`max_num_seqs` too high for the active working set; combined with aggressive timeout produced retry-amplification and triggered kvcache paging storm.
maya: adding action items to draft: - enforce config gating for cont-batch params (approve flag for PRs) - add canary guardrail metric: kv_evictions_total > X triggers automated rollback - add alert for config changes tagged 'experiment' - add SLO check for batch timeouts vs avg page-in latency.
jamie: CS follow-up: collect list of impacted customers and communicate RCA and timeline. also offer instance of dedicated capacity for one high-touch customer temporarily.
alyssa: assigning owners: diego -> postmortem and rollback automation; maya -> config gating + canary guardrails; jamie -> customer comms + impacted list; i'll close incident when postmortem + comms drafted.
incident-bot: Incident CB-2024-7453 moved to RESOLVED at 2024-08-14T03:12:03Z by alyssa. Duration: 41m7s.
alyssa: final notes: hotfix prevented further customer impact; root cause conditional: experiment config got promoted into prod without canary limits. We'll keep timeout conservative while we implement guardrails.
jamie: will post update to customers in 30m with mitigation summary and next steps.
(threads/attachments: logs, prom queries, and kubectl command snippets posted inline)
